children: The NZX 50 was almost flat, trading around 13,823 in Tuesday morning trade, after rising in the previous session, as gains in consumer discretionary, financials, and real estate offset declines in materials, and healthcare.
The broader index remained at its highest level since September 7, touched a day earlier, as traders were cautious ahead of the Trump-Xi summit later this week.
Caution was also evident as traders continued to monitor developments in the Middle East conflict and the impact on oil prices amid efforts to ease tensions.
On a positive note, Wall Street closed in the green overnight, buoyed by strong tech stocks, while oil prices and US Treasury yields eased.

Colonial Motor rose 1.7%, Summerset Group climbed 1.2%, Channel Infrastructure gained 1.1%, and Scales Corporation advanced 0.9%, while Fisher & Paykel, Freightways Group, and Mainfreight fell 1.2%, 0.6%, and 0.4%, respectively.

title: New Zealand Stocks Little Changed in Morning Trade
